-87.64440,41.89900.name: Fertility Centers of Illinois-River North IVF
-87.64440,41.89900.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Jennifer E. Hirshfeld-Cytron, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-8.49269,33.24374.name: Clinique Les Palmiers
-8.49269,33.24374.desc: A clinic mapped in OpenStreetMap as offering fertility treatment. OpenStreetMap holds what somebody chose to map, so a country with few points here may be thinly mapped rather than thinly served. That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

78.87840,18.03098.name: Vivo Bio Tech Limited
78.87840,18.03098.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-99.63334,19.21468.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: http://clinicainfertilidadtoluca.com/. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere. No street address resolved, so this point is the city or the country rather than the centre.

12.54629,55.68459.name: National Veterinary Institute
12.54629,55.68459.desc: A BSL3+ laboratory, operational. Run by Technical University of Denmark. It is categorised as a university laboratory, working on human health. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

-68.11930,-16.48970.name: Comité Nacional de Bioseguridad
-68.11930,-16.48970.desc: Bolivia’s biosafety committee, in a country that permits engineered soy but has resisted expanding approvals under pressure from both agribusiness and indigenous organisations. The dispute is unusually explicit about whose land and whose seed is at stake.

-71.04800,42.35200.name: Fidelity and index funds — passive ownership of the sector
-71.04800,42.35200.desc: Index funds hold large stakes in nearly every listed company on this map at once, because they hold the index rather than choosing companies. The consequence is that the same handful of managers are simultaneously among the largest owners of firms that compete with each other — a concentration produced by a savings product, examined by no merger review, and voted at every annual meeting.

-0.08700,51.52400.name: OpenCorporates — across jurisdictions at once
-0.08700,51.52400.desc: The same lookup across dozens of national registers in one search, which is what you need when a company operates under different names in different countries — the normal arrangement in this industry. It is also the practical answer to a change of name, which otherwise breaks a trail entirely.
